answer: Correlated equivocation links bonded identities through shared evidence, so a swarm of k participants incurs pairwise penalties proportional to k(k−1)/2, hence O(k²), rather than k separate flat fines. Upon detection, an exponential multiplier in capital loss is applied to the bonded swarm, with asymmetric depreciation preventing rapid recovery. Splitting control across sybils therefore increases exposure, not safety; the quartz kernel records proofs and the jetty escrow holds collateral pending attribution.
